title: Settling an Approved Refund on a Vacation Package
content:
An approved refund on one of Wanderlane's Vacation Package Products settles in the form the product prescribes: money to the card, or a future travel credit voucher, never both and never a mixture.

**When a payout line may be raised.** A payout line is raised only while the package record stands at cancelled or completed. The status carried on the package record settles this, and a package standing at quoted, deposit held, confirmed, travelling or closed is outside the two states in which a payout may be raised.

**How long the settlement takes.** The settlement takes the product's processing time, counted in business days from the day the refund was approved, excluding weekends and public holidays in the lead traveller's country of residence.

**A clause no longer in force.** "Each payout is raised against the original ledger line it reverses, so a package with a deposit and several instalments settles as several payouts." That clause is **no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis of the vacation packages charter; it is recorded here so that the withdrawn wording can be recognised.

**The ceilings on a payout.** A payout may never exceed the amount that original line actually collected, and the sum of a package's payouts may never exceed the amount paid on it.

**Where a supplier fails.** Where a supplier within the package fails financially, the protected amount is settled under the product's financial protection whatever its ordinary refund form.

## Both sides of the ceilings, on hypothetical particulars

Where an original line collected 600.00 USD, a payout of 600.00 USD against it is at the ceiling and stands; a payout of 601.00 USD against it exceeds the amount that line collected and does not. Where a package has taken 2,400.00 USD in all, its payouts together may reach 2,400.00 USD and no more, however many lines they are raised on.

superseded_clauses: Each payout is raised against the original ledger line it reverses, so a package with a deposit and several instalments settles as several payouts.
